# Grid row selection treats a record keyed 0 as no record

## Context

Found while triaging #21132. That PR adds `Neo.grid.View#selectedRecords`, which resolves each selected row id through `BaseModel#getRowRecord`. Under `useInternalId: false`, row ids are the record keys, and a key of `0` is valid data (an array index, a database row).

Probe at #21132's head `164294f3c2`, using the harness of `test/playwright/unit/grid/ViewOwnedSelectionModel.spec.mjs`: store keys `0`–`4`, `useInternalId: false`, `RowModel`. `painted` lists the selected rows each of the three bodies paints:

```
key 1 (control):                selectedRows [1]  selectedRecords [1]  painted [[1],[1],[1]]
key 0:                          selectedRows [0]                       painted [[],[],[]]
                                store.get(0).id 0  getRowRecord(0) null  selectedRecords.length 0
ArrowDown from key 0:           selectedRows [0]
ArrowUp from key 1 onto key 0:  selectedRows [1]
ArrowDown from key 1 (control): selectedRows [2]
```

#21132 touches none of the code below. The same checks are on `dev` `2404340dfa`.

## The Problem

A click selects the row keyed `0`, because `RowModel#onRowClick` has no guard, so the model holds `0`. Every later step reads `0` as "no id":

- the row is never painted as selected, in any body;
- `getRowRecord(0)` returns `null` although `store.get(0)` resolves the record, so `View#selectedRecords` silently leaves out a record that exists and is selected;
- `ArrowUp` and `ArrowDown` can neither land on the row nor move away from it.

No shipped grid sets `useInternalId: false` (`git grep` over `apps/` and `examples/`). This hits applications that opt in and have a record keyed `0`.

## The Architectural Reality

- `Design authority: "Resolves a record from an ID (PK or internalId)."` (`src/selection/grid/BaseModel.mjs:424`, the JSDoc of `getRowRecord`). A key of `0` is a PK.
- Six lines in `src/selection/grid` test a row id for truthiness (`dev` `2404340dfa`):
  - `BaseModel.mjs:172`, `updateRows`: `if (!recordIds || recordIds.length === 0) return;`. A scalar `0` returns before any body repaints.
  - `BaseModel.mjs:429`, `getRowRecord`: `if (!id) return null;`.
  - `RowModel.mjs:117` and `CellRowModel.mjs:61`, `onNavKeyRow`: `me.selectedRows[0] || view.getRecordId(store.getAt(0))`. A selected `0` falls back to the first record, so navigation from a row keyed `0` that is not first starts at the wrong row.
  - `RowModel.mjs:133` and `CellRowModel.mjs:77`, `onNavKeyRow`: `if (recordId)`. A target row keyed `0` is never selected.
- Past these checks, `0` works: `store.get(0)` resolves the record (probe above), and `Row` paints by `selectedRows.includes(recordId)` (`src/grid/Row.mjs:488`).
- `updateCells`' `if (!logicalIds …)` (`BaseModel.mjs:242`) is unaffected, because logical cell ids are non-empty strings.

## The Fix

Read a row id as missing only when it is `null` or `undefined`. `== null` is the codebase's idiom.

1. `BaseModel#updateRows`: `if (recordIds == null || recordIds.length === 0) return`.
2. `BaseModel#getRowRecord`: `if (id == null) return null`.
3. `RowModel#onNavKeyRow` and `CellRowModel#onNavKeyRow`: `me.selectedRows[0] ?? view.getRecordId(store.getAt(0))`, and `if (recordId != null)`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Under `useInternalId: false`, `selectRow(0)` paints the row keyed `0` in every body that renders it.
- [ ] `getRowRecord(0)` returns the record keyed `0`. `getRowRecord(null)` and `getRowRecord(undefined)` still return `null`.
- [ ] Under `RowModel` and under `CellRowModel`, `ArrowDown` moves from the row keyed `0` to the next row, and `ArrowUp` from the next row lands on it. Both hold when the row keyed `0` is not the store's first record.
- [ ] Unit specs in `test/playwright/unit/grid/ViewOwnedSelectionModel.spec.mjs` cover each box above and fail on `dev` before the fix. Its `createStore()` already builds keys `0`–`4` (pass a `key` function to move `0` off the first row), and `createGrid()` sets `useInternalId: false`. Run them with `npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/grid/ViewOwnedSelectionModel.spec.mjs`.
- [ ] If #21132 is merged when this is picked up, a spec also shows `grid.view.selectedRecords` returning the record keyed `0`.

## Out of Scope

- Grids with `useInternalId: true`: internal ids are non-empty strings.
- The table family (`src/selection/table/`), which keeps its own row ids. Its `if (rowId)` checks (`RowModel.mjs:103`, `CellRowModel.mjs:85`) were not probed.
- Keyboard navigation in an empty store.

## Avoided Traps

- **Treating a key of `0` as invalid data.** The store resolves it and the row paints by it; only these checks reject it.
- **Fixing `getRowRecord` alone.** The row would still not paint (`updateRows`), and navigation from a row keyed `0` that is not first would still start at the first record (`selectedRows[0] || …`).

## Related

- #21132 / #21102: `View#selectedRecords` resolves through `getRowRecord`.
- #18626: the View owns the selection model.
